config.title: Grid vs Flex: when to use which

intro.title: Grid vs Flex: when to use which
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout to understand when to use CSS Grid versus CSS Flexbox. You'll learn the core concept of choosing the right layout model based on whether you need one-dimensional (Flexbox) or two-dimensional (Grid) control. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid for overall page structure and CSS Flexbox for aligning items within sections. By the end, you'll be able to decide which tool to use for common layout tasks, applying your knowledge through hands-on coding exercises.
intro.usecase: Understanding when to use CSS Grid versus Flexbox is essential for building modern, responsive layouts in real-world applications. For example, a product dashboard uses Grid to create a two-dimensional layout of cards, charts, and widgets arranged in rows and columns, while a navigation menu or a filter bar relies on Flexbox for one-dimensional alignment of items horizontally or vertically. Developers choose Grid for overall page structure, like a news article with a sidebar and main content, and Flexbox for components within those sections, such as a button group or a list of tags. Mastering this distinction allows you to efficiently build complex interfaces like admin panels, e-commerce product grids, or interactive data tables that adapt seamlessly across devices.

objectives: Construct a one-dimensional layout using Flexbox to align items horizontally.
Implement a two-dimensional grid layout using CSS Grid to arrange items in rows and columns.
Apply Flexbox properties to control spacing and distribution of items within a container.
Configure Grid areas to define and place content in specific regions of a layout.
Manipulate a navigation bar using Flexbox for inline alignment and responsive behavior.
Integrate Grid and Flexbox within a single layout to leverage their respective strengths.
Update an existing layout by switching from Flexbox to Grid to achieve a more complex structure.

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for comparing Grid and Flex
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with a container div and two child sections - one for Grid examples and one for Flex examples
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure that includes a container and two sections inside it
steps.seedCode:
/* Create your HTML structure here */
/* Add a container with two sections */
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the foundation for comparing Grid and Flex with semantic HTML containers
successCriteria: A container div with two child sections (one for Grid, one for Flex) is created
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have a container with two sections - one for Grid and one for Flex.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a container with two sections to hold your Grid and Flex examples.

steps.title: Add basic styling to visualize the containers
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to give the container a light gray background, 20px padding, and a 2px solid black border. Also give each section inside it a white background, 10px padding, and a 1px solid gray border.
steps.hint: Use the selector for the container element and apply background-color, padding, and border properties. Then target the sections inside with another selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container and sections will have visible borders and background colors, making them distinguishable on the page.
successCriteria: The CSS includes rules for the container with background-color, padding, and border properties, and rules for sections with their own background, padding, and border.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both the container and sections have background colors, padding, and borders as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rules are missing or incorrect. Ensure you're targeting the container and sections with appropriate selectors and applying the specified properties.

steps.title: Create a one-dimensional layout with Flexbox
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the flex container class to apply display: flex and set flex-direction to row.
steps.hint: Use the display property with value 'flex' and flex-direction with value 'row' to create a horizontal layout.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex container will be ready to arrange child items horizontally in a single row.
successCriteria: The .flex-container rule includes display: flex and flex-direction: row.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both display: flex and flex-direction: row are included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex container rule is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added display: flex and flex-direction: row.

steps.title: Create a two-dimensional layout with CSS Grid
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a class named '.grid-container' with 'display: grid' and define both rows and columns using 'grid-template-rows' and 'grid-template-columns' properties.
steps.hint: Use 'grid-template-rows' and 'grid-template-columns' to create a 2x2 grid layout. You can use values like '1fr' for equal-sized rows and columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for '.grid-container' is created with display: grid and both rows and columns defined, enabling a two-dimensional layout.
successCriteria: The '.grid-container' rule includes 'display: grid', 'grid-template-rows', and 'grid-template-columns' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've included all three properties: 'display: grid', 'grid-template-rows', and 'grid-template-columns' in your '.grid-container' rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your CSS syntax. You need to create a '.grid-container' class with 'display: grid' and define both rows and columns using 'grid-template-rows' and 'grid-template-columns'.

steps.title: Compare Flexbox alignment properties
steps.instruction: Inside the .flex-container rule, add the justify-content property with value 'space-between' and the align-items property with value 'center' to demonstrate Flexbox alignment.
steps.hint: Add these two properties inside the existing .flex-container rule to align items along both axes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Flexbox container will now align its items with equal space between them horizontally and center them vertically.
successCriteria: The .flex-container rule includes both justify-content: space-between and align-items: center properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both justify-content and align-items properties to the .flex-container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're adding the properties inside the existing .flex-container rule, not creating a new rule.

steps.title: Compare Grid alignment properties
steps.instruction: Add a .grid-container class with display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), and grid-template-rows: repeat(2, 100px) to create a grid structure for alignment demonstration.
steps.hint: Start by defining the grid container with display: grid and setting up a 3-column, 2-row grid structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A grid container class is created with a defined grid structure of 3 columns and 2 rows.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class includes display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), and grid-template-rows: repeat(2, 100px).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include all three properties: display: grid, grid-template-columns, and grid-template-rows.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid container structure isn't complete. Remember to use display: grid and define both columns and rows for the grid.

steps.title: Demonstrate content-based sizing with Flexbox
steps.instruction: Add varying content to the flex items inside the .flex-container to show how Flexbox naturally sizes items based on content.
steps.hint: Inside each flex item, add different amounts of text or elements to create varying content widths.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will have different widths based on their content, demonstrating Flexbox's content-based sizing behavior.
successCriteria: Flex items contain varying amounts of content
Items display with different widths based on their content
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some content, but try to make the content differences more noticeable between items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex items don't show clear content-based sizing. Add significantly different amounts of content to each item.

steps.title: Demonstrate explicit sizing with CSS Grid
steps.instruction: In the .grid-container rule, add explicit grid track definitions using grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows to create a 2x2 grid with fixed and flexible sizes.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-columns: 100px 1fr; and grid-template-rows: 50px 2fr; to define two columns (one fixed at 100px, one flexible) and two rows (one fixed at 50px, one flexible).
steps.expectedOutcome: The .grid-container rule will have explicit grid track definitions that demonstrate fixed and flexible sizing using px and fr units.
successCriteria: The .grid-container rule includes grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties with at least one fixed size (px) and one flexible size (fr).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows with at least one fixed (px) and one flexible (fr) value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid container needs explicit track definitions. Add grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows properties with fixed and flexible sizes.

steps.title: Create a responsive navigation with Flexbox
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .nav class that uses Flexbox to create a horizontal navigation bar with items spaced evenly.
steps.hint: Set display: flex, justify-content: space-evenly, and align-items: center on the .nav class.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new .nav CSS rule is added with Flexbox properties to create a horizontal navigation layout.
successCriteria: The .nav rule includes display: flex, justify-content: space-evenly, and align-items: center.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your .nav rule includes all three required Flexbox properties: display: flex, justify-content: space-evenly, and align-items: center.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation rule is missing or doesn't use the required Flexbox properties. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create a card layout with CSS Grid
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule for a .card-grid container that uses CSS Grid to create a responsive card layout with 3 columns and a 20px gap.
steps.hint: Use display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), and gap: 20px to create the grid structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS Grid layout for cards with 3 equal columns and consistent spacing between cards.
successCriteria: The .card-grid rule includes display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), and gap: 20px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include all three properties: display: grid, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), and gap: 20px.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction again. You need to create a CSS Grid layout with 3 columns and spacing between cards.
